Thank you for the explanations 🙏
I agree that for people that don't speak Hebrew at all (neither their local partners) opening an Osek Patur/Zair might be somewhat difficult due to the documents being printed in Hebrew.

But for those that can deal with the Hebrew, whether with the help of their partners or an AI translation, the process is actually not very difficult. 

1. After you get the B1, you first need to open a local bank account. Bring your passport and show them the B1 visa. After they open your account, ask the bank representative to print for you an official bank statement that validates you are the owner of the bank account.
2. After you have a bank account under your name, you need to go to your local Ma'am (מע״מ) office with your partner. Bring your ID and the official bank statement that validates you are the owner of the bank account.
3. Ma'am will create a fake business ID number for you and give you your Osek Patur certificate.
4. Once you finish with Ma'am, you will need to visit your local Mas Hachnasa (מס הכנסה) office and register as Osek Zair. Don't forget to bring your business Osek Patur certificate from Ma'am and your bank account details.

These are the main steps when doing the process alone. 

Once you run your business, submitting your annual business reports for Osek Patur/Zair are also not too hard, so if you don't mind doing it yourself, it can save you a few thousand shekels per year.
